reference_drawer.title: 📖 Similarity Criteria Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Theorems and criteria for triangle similarity.

items.rule: AA/AAA, SAS, and SSS are standard triangle similarity criteria.
items.example: Match corresponding vertices before forming side ratios.

items.rule: Two proportional corresponding sides and their included equal angle establish similarity.
items.example: The equal angle must be between the two compared sides.

items.rule: All three corresponding side ratios must be equal.
Altitude to the hypotenuse produces similar triangles and geometric-mean relations.
items.example: Use the product of the two hypotenuse segments.

items.rule: Shadows and mirror arrangements form similar right triangles.
items.example: Keep height paired with the corresponding shadow or mirror distance.

concepts.title: 1. Similarity Criteria (AAA, SSS, SAS)
concepts.subtitle: Conditions for similar triangles
concepts.summary: AA/AAA uses corresponding equal angles, SAS uses two proportional sides with the included equal angle, and SSS uses three proportional side ratios.

points.text: SAS: two proportional sides plus included equal angle.
SSS: all three corresponding side ratios equal.

concepts.title: 4. Right-Triangle Similarity Relations
concepts.subtitle: Altitude to hypotenuse
concepts.summary: An altitude from the right angle to the hypotenuse creates similar triangles and geometric-mean relations.

points.text: Use the two leg geometric means.

concepts.formula: AD^2 = BD\cdot DC,\; AB^2 = BD\cdot BC,\; AC^2 = DC\cdot BC
